note: Synthetic. Nothing ran: every tree is mocked recorder files, and each "60 s window" is arithmetic. It shows what the real scorer does with those bytes and says nothing about any host. Not a capacity observation. Outcomes are not scripted: each comes from the real prover and scorer over the bytes the fake guest exported.

policy.boundaries: Tick counts and socket drops are evaluated over the widest and the narrowest interval the clocks allow. A verdict must hold for both, or it stays unknown.

enet_loss.definition: one bin per second from the window start. A bot counts once per bin: the mean of its readings in that bin, or else its nearest in-window reading within 2 s of the bin, labelled borrowed. A bin's value is the mean over the bots still owed there. Every bin must stay strictly below the limit.
enet_loss.estimator: ENet smoothed reliable-command loss estimate, updated at most once per 10 s epoch. Not a measured fraction of datagrams dropped.

policy.generator_evidence: A failed gate or a crash establishes nothing over a generator not proven valid. Every reason the prover draws from the swarm's own files stands: a server's missing data can be the consequence of its demonstrated crash, and a generator's cannot.

input.definition: per bot: sent over its own scheduled grid slots in the window, in integers. Exactly 99 percent is valid. A disconnected bot is held to the part it was connected for, less the one slot the disconnect can interrupt.

policy.oom: The host-wide kernel OOM count is a diagnostic and never explains a process exit. A count for the run's unit names no process, because the kernel raises it before the SIGKILL and another member can be counted and still alive at any read, so it never explains a process exit either. A game SIGKILL is out_of_memory only when the kernel counted exactly one OOM kill local to a leaf cgroup of the run's unit, made fresh for the game before it started, holding the sealed game and nobody else at every read, between a baseline of zero and a read right after the reap. Anything less stays killed_with_no_cause_on_record.

ramp.definition: A ramp can fail and can never pass. Its failure needs the supervised swarm and game identities, a kick only of a bot both sides recorded as authenticated, and zero generator socket drops proven on every opened socket by a counter read certainly after the abort. A read that may precede the abort, or a socket no such read saw, leaves the generator not proven.

rtt_quantile.definition: empirical nearest rank: sort every in-window sample of every bot into one pool of n, take the value at 1-based rank ceil(95 n / 100). No interpolation, and never an average of per-bot quantiles.
rtt_quantile.estimator: ENet smoothed mean round trip time in whole milliseconds
